text: An individual is said to be resident in India in any previous year, if he has been in India during that year for a period or periods amounting in all to one hundred and eighty-two days or more.
Derived rule: an individual is resident if days_in_india_fy is at least 182.

chapter.title: DETERMINATION OF TAX IN CERTAIN SPECIAL CASES

text: Where the total income of an assessee includes any income chargeable under the head capital gains, arising from the transfer of a short-term capital asset being an equity share in a company or a unit of an equity oriented fund or a unit of a business trust, and the transaction of sale of such equity share or unit is chargeable to securities transaction tax under Chapter VII of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2004, the tax payable by the assessee on the total income shall be the aggregate of the amount of income-tax calculated on such short-term capital gains at the rate of twenty per cent.
notes: Rate changed from 15% to 20% by Finance Act 2024 w.e.f. 23.07.2024

chapter.title: DETERMINATION OF TAX IN CERTAIN SPECIAL CASES

text: Derived eligibility: section 111A applies only if STT was paid on the transfer of the listed equity share or unit.
notes: Must be true for 111A rate to apply; otherwise normal slab rate applies

chapter.title: DETERMINATION OF TAX IN CERTAIN SPECIAL CASES

text: Where the total income of an assessee includes any income chargeable under the head capital gains, arising from the transfer of a long-term capital asset being an equity share in a company or a unit of an equity oriented fund or a unit of a business trust, and the transaction of sale of such equity share or unit is chargeable to securities transaction tax, the tax payable by the assessee on the total income shall include income-tax on such long-term capital gains exceeding one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees at the rate of twelve and one-half per cent.
notes: Exemption raised from 1 lakh to 1.25 lakh; rate raised from 10% to 12.5% by Finance Act 2024 w.e.f. 23.07.2024

chapter.title: DETERMINATION OF TAX IN CERTAIN SPECIAL CASES

text: Derived rule: an equity share in a listed company is a long-term capital asset if held for more than twelve months.
notes: Listed equity LTCA threshold is 12 months (not 24 months applicable to unlisted shares)

chapter.title: DETERMINATION OF TAX IN CERTAIN SPECIAL CASES

text: Derived eligibility: section 112A applies only if STT was paid both at acquisition and at transfer of the equity share or unit.
notes: Both acquisition and transfer must be STT-paid for 112A to apply

chapter.title: DETERMINATION OF TAX IN CERTAIN SPECIAL CASES

text: The amount of long-term capital gains of one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees shall not be chargeable to tax under section 112A.
notes: Raised from 100000 to 125000 by Finance Act 2024

text: Any person responsible for paying to a resident any income by way of dividends shall, at the time of payment thereof, deduct income-tax thereon at the rate of ten per cent.
notes: TDS @ 10% on dividend income; DDT abolished by Finance Act 2020

text: Where the recipient does not furnish PAN to the payer, TDS shall be deducted at the higher of the rate specified in the relevant provision or twenty per cent.
notes: Section 206AA applies; 20% TDS if PAN not furnished

text: Any person, not being an individual or a Hindu undivided family, responsible for paying to a resident any income by way of interest other than interest on securities shall deduct income-tax at the rate of ten per cent where the aggregate of interest income credited or paid during the financial year exceeds forty thousand rupees in case the payer is a banking company.
notes: Threshold raised from 10000 to 40000 by Finance Act 2019 for banks/co-ops/post offices; 50000 for senior citizens

text: The threshold for TDS on interest from banking companies is fifty thousand rupees for a senior citizen (an individual resident who is of the age of sixty years or more at any time during the relevant previous year).
notes: Age 60+ at any time during FY qualifies; threshold 50000 not 40000

text: In computing the total income of an assessee, being an individual or a Hindu undivided family, there shall be deducted, in accordance with and subject to the provisions of this section, the whole of the amount paid or deposited in the previous year, being the aggregate of the sums referred to in sub-section (2), as does not exceed one lakh fifty thousand rupees.
notes: Cap is 1.5 lakh; has not changed since FY 2014-15

text: In computing the total income of an assessee, being an individual or a Hindu undivided family, there shall be deducted such sum as specified in sub-section (2) on account of any premium paid to effect or keep in force an insurance on the health of the assessee or his family, not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees.
notes: 25000 for self+family; 50000 if senior citizen; additional 25000/50000 for parents

text: In case of a senior citizen, the deduction limit under section 80D for health insurance premium shall be fifty thousand rupees.

An assessee, being an individual resident in India, whose total income does not exceed five hundred thousand rupees, shall be entitled to a deduction from the amount of income-tax (as computed before allowing the deductions under this Chapter) of an amount equal to hundred per cent of such income-tax or twelve thousand five hundred rupees, whichever is less.
notes: Old regime: total income <= 5L gets full rebate up to 12500. New regime: <= 7L gets rebate up to 25000 under 87A

text: Under the new tax regime (section 115BAC), the rebate under section 87A is available up to twenty-five thousand rupees for individuals with total income not exceeding seven hundred thousand rupees.
notes: Default regime is new regime from FY 2023-24 onwards

part.title: INTEREST FOR NON-PAYMENT OF ADVANCE TAX

text: Where, in any financial year, an assessee who is liable to pay advance tax has failed to pay such tax or where the advance tax paid by such assessee is less than ninety per cent of the assessed tax, the assessee shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of one per cent for every month or part of a month.
notes: 1% per month interest on shortfall below 90% of assessed tax

text: Every person, being an individual whose total income of the previous year exceeds the maximum amount which is not chargeable to income-tax, shall furnish a return of his income. The basic exemption limit for individuals below 60 years is two lakh fifty thousand rupees.
For a senior citizen (age 60 to 80 years), the basic exemption limit is three lakh rupees. For a super senior citizen (age above 80 years), the basic exemption limit is five lakh rupees.
notes: Age computed as of 1st April of the relevant FY
